title: Is it safe to use rice cereal/rice cakes/puffs for babies (arsenic)?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.outcome: Infant rice products as an inorganic arsenic source
grade.basis: The EFSA opinion covers rice products. Product concentrations for cereal, cakes, and puffs were not verified.

answerHtml: Rice and rice products are identified as a dietary source of inorganic arsenic in the EFSA 2024 opinion recorded in the corpus. This corpus does not contain a verified arsenic concentration for infant rice cereal, rice cakes, or puffs, so it does not state a safe serving. The reference point of 0.06 µg/kg body weight per day is a toxicological benchmark, not a product limit.

sections.heading: What is not available
sections.html: No infant serving size and no micrograms per serving were verified. Brand names are not ranked.

heavyMetalIndexHtml: Heavy Metal Index: infant rice cereal. This Heavy Metal Index URL returned HTTP 200 on 15 October 2026. Figures on this page are not copied from that index. They come from the sources named above.
buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
